The defending Cup Series champion scored his 35th career victory Sunday and his third in the past seven races. Nate Ryan , Larson has opened a 73-point lead over Denny Hamlin with two races remaining in the season. item.title: ‘Let’s Just Go To Flag Football’ — Packers Superstar Micah Parsons Takes Aim at Refs’ Questionable Decisions in Favor of Lions
item.description: ‘Let’s Just Go To Flag Football’ — Packers Superstar Micah Parsons Takes Aim at Refs’ Questionable Decisions in Favor of Lions Micah Parsons is still waiting for his first snap of the 2026 season, but the Green Bay Packers’ star pass rusher found a way to make himself heard Sunday. Parsons went after the NFL and its officiating department over roughing-the-passer calls. It came on a day the Packers drew two of those flags in a 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions, which ended with Jake Bates’ 22-yard field goal as time expired at Ford Field. Micah Parsons Takes the Roughing Debate Straight to the League Parsons is still on the reserve/physically unable to perform list as he recovers from a torn ACL and meniscus damage suffered last December. He tagged both the league and its officiating account and minced no words: “Let’s just go to flag football if every time a QB gets touched it’s roughing the passer!” NFL legend Tom Brady, calling the game, also had a blunt reaction to one of the roughing flags. “My goodness. What is that?” he said on the FOX broadcast before adding, “It’s definitely not roughing the passer.” The first of Sunday’s roughing flags came in the third quarter with Green Bay trailing 17-14. item.title: Top takeaways from Ravens’ Week 7 loss to Bengals
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Cincinnati Bengals halfback Samaje Perine (34) holds back Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey (44) during the second half at M&T Bank Stadium. For better and for worse, Lamar Jackson cures virtually all ills on the offensive side of the ball. He keeps his teammates focused and makes the impossible plays when they are necessary. But who is that on the Ravens defense? They have a laundry list of names – Kyle Hamilton, Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Calais Campbell, Nnamdi Madubuike – but they are all polished, well-spoke players, perhaps to a fault. Who is on the sidelines holding their teammates accountable – loudly, aggressively, if need be? Ray Lewis, Ed Reed, and Terrell Suggs may be nearly impossible to live up to, but they represent the standard nonetheless. Seeing some of those legends chime in during the game on social media made me cringe in embarrassment for the team. And, yes, the coaches deserve a glance here, too. item.title: Texas football's potential top 10 draft pick out for the year
item.description: Texas football's potential top 10 draft pick out for the year originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Texas Longhorns earned a 34-27 victory over Ole Miss, but the win came at a significant cost as injuries continue to threaten the No. 11 Longhorns' season. Left tackle Trevor Goosby will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a left knee injury in the first quarter Saturday against the Rebels, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel . The 6-foot-7, 325-pound senior was carted off the field, with backup Andre Cojoe taking over for the rest of the game. Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian expressed concern after the victory, telling reporters the injury did not "look very good." Goosby's absence is a major setback for Texas, which has five regular-season games remaining. He started 22 games over the past three seasons and earned first-team All-SEC honors. He also entered the season as a preseason first-team All-American and a projected top offensive tackle prospect in the 2027 NFL draft. He previously dealt with a bone bruise in his left knee during preseason camp in August but returned to start the Longhorns' first seven games. Texas also lost wide receiver Cam Coleman to an apparent shoulder injury against Ole Miss. Coleman, a highly regarded transfer from Auburn, has recorded 348 receiving yards and six touchdowns on 21 catches this season. His status moving forward remains uncertain. The Longhorns were already without pass rusher Colin Simmons and running back Hollywood Smothers. Despite the growing injury concerns, Texas climbed eight spots to No. 11 in Sunday's AP Top 25 after securing its second victory over a top-10 opponent. The Longhorns improved to 5-2 overall and 2-2 in SEC play. However, Goosby's season-ending injury puts additional pressure on an offensive line that must protect Arch Manning and establish consistency down the stretch. Texas hosts Mississippi State on Saturday (7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN). item.title: Kiah Stokes passes Brittney Griner with a WNBA Finals record
item.description: Kiah Stokes passes Brittney Griner with a WNBA Finals record originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kiah Stokes made history while helping the Golden State Valkyries put the WNBA Finals back on level ground. In Game 4 against the Atlanta Dream , Stokes collected 16 rebounds and blocked three shots as Golden State earned a 67-62 road victory. Those blocks pushed Stokes to 14 for the series, giving her the most in a single WNBA Finals. She moved past Brittney Griner and Sylvia Fowles, who had each recorded 12. Stokes also became the first player in Finals history to register at least three blocks in four consecutive games. It was the kind of performance that does not need a high-scoring line to dominate the conversation. The game was tight, the total was low, and every possession around the basket mattered. Stokes gave Golden State a major presence near the rim while also controlling the glass. The record has history behind it Griner set the previous mark in the 2014 Finals, recording 12 blocks in only two games before an injury kept her out of Game 3. Fowles matched that total in 2017. Stokes now stands alone at the top of the list after four straight games of disrupting shots. Kiah Stokes in first four games of the Finals: 11.3 RPG 3.5 BPG Set the WNBA record for most total blocks in a Finals series with 14. https://t.co/eHTZHA0mxK — Underdog WNBA (@UnderdogWNBA) October 24, 2026 A block is the most visible part of rim protection, but the larger impact often comes before the shot. A defender who is waiting near the basket can force a player to hesitate, alter a layup or pass the ball away. That pressure can reshape an entire possession without showing up in the box score. Stokes’ presence has given the Valkyries a defensive foundation as they try to win the franchise’s first championship. Golden State had fallen behind in the series after Game 3, then responded with a road win to tie it at 2-2 and reclaim momentum. MORE : Dream's Angel Reese made WNBA Finals history despite Game 1 loss A record and a series still to win The Finals record belongs to Stokes regardless of what happens next, but the series gives her a chance to extend it. Game 5 presents another opportunity for Golden State to take the lead, while Atlanta will need to find ways to attack without allowing Stokes to control the paint. The achievement also spotlights a player whose impact can be overlooked when championship coverage gravitates toward scoring stars. Stokes’ 14 blocks reflect timing, discipline and consistency across four high-pressure games. Golden State is now even with Atlanta, and Stokes has helped make defense the Valkyries’ most compelling story. If she continues to protect the rim at this level, the record could keep growing right alongside the team’s championship hopes. item.title: Doncic dominates for Lakers as James' Sixers fall to Pistons
item.description: Luka Doncic is now the undisputed superstar of the Los Angeles Lakers since LeBron James departed for Philadelphia (CHRIS GARDNER) Luka Doncic scored a monster 52 points as the Los Angeles Lakers maintained their perfect start to life after LeBron James with a 132-123 defeat of the Utah Jazz. Now the undisputed superstar of the Lakers since James departed this summer for Philadelphia, Doncic also provided 10 assists and eight rebounds in a masterful performance, with eight three-pointers and two steals. Doncic was supported by Austin Reaves, who had 29 points, as the visitors pulled decisively clear in the last four minutes of a game they had trailed for long periods. "It's one of the best feelings -- down the stretch, tight game, hitting those threes," said Doncic. "Played the basketball we know how to play. We are learning our lesson...we cannot start games like this any more." It was the first 50-point game by an NBA player this season. Slovenian point guard Doncic was the league's top scorer last season. After cruising to comfortable opening wins against the Golden State Warriors and city rival Clippers, the Lakers overcame their first real adversity of the nascent season in Salt Lake City. Utah led nearly the entire first half, pulling as many as 18 points clear, with Finland's Lauri Markkanen on scintillating form. But the Lakers rallied. A Doncic three-point pullup shot with seconds remaining in the second quarter gave Los Angeles a slender lead at the interval. The Jazz had inched back in front with just over four minutes remaining, when another Doncic trey tied up the score 116-116. From there Doncic and Reaves were relentless, outscoring the entire Jazz offense in the final quarter between them, as the new-look Lakers moved to a perfect 3-0 start. "We have a tight group. Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams was off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 NBA season, as he was fully healthy after an injury-riddled 2025-26 campaign. In a tragic turn of events, Williams suffered a gruesome lower-body injury late in their 108-101 win against the Los Angeles Clippers . The Thunder 's medical staff had to take him off the court on a stretcher, so the injury does not look good. It is yet another bad chapter in Williams' career, as he has struggled with injuries throughout his time in the league. However, that has been dialed up to 100 ever since the Thunder won the title in 2025. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gets visibly emotional after Jalen Williams' injury Ever since Williams entered the league in 2022, he has been close to Gilgeous-Alexander. They have become the Thunder's star duo, as they quickly became the best players during the Thunder's rise to the top of the NBA. On and off the court, Gilgeous-Alexander and Williams have been close, so that is why it's hard for the former to keep seeing his teammate get injured. Sunday night's injury was the latest chapter in Williams' struggles because he was finally healthy after constant spells on the sidelines in the year prior. MORE: The latest injury update on Jalen Williams after he was stretchered out of the game Now, it seems the Thunder have to deal with it all over again. It has hurt Williams and his teammates even harder this time because it looked like a gruesome injury, and the players empathize with their teammate who has to go through physical therapy yet again. "I just feel bad for him. Nothing more than that... We don't have no choice; this is what we signed up for. Obviously, it's gonna be tough without a player like that. He's not gone forever; he'll be back better than ever, we know it. We just have to hold the fort down until he comes back," Gilgeous-Alexander said in his post-game interview after the win vs. the Clippers . It will be tough for the Thunder to deal with this again, but thankfully, they have a talented roster. Head coach Mark Daigneault is spoiled for choice with his talented group of players, but he would prefer having a healthy Williams in the rotation. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Serge Gnabry thinks Harry Kane has ‘done enough’ to win Ballon d’Or
item.description: Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images | Getty Images The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner will be revealed on October 26th. According to popular opinion, the title for the world’s best footballer is a two-horse race between Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal. Both players have made a strong case to win the award. Harry Kane won the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and Franz Beckenbauer Supercup with Bayern Munich last season, producing his highest-scoring season of all time . The Englishman also played a pivotal role in England’s third-place finish at the World Cup. Lamine Yam al also produced the most prolific season of his career, scoring 25 goals and assisting 20 more acros s all competitions. The 19-year-old won La Liga, the Copa del Rey, and the Supe rcopa de España, and also secured his first World Cup with Spain. Little separates Kane and Yamal on their charges t o win the Ballon d’Or. But Bayern’s Serge Gnabry believes his teammate has done enough to pip the Spanish phenom. “It would be lovely if he were to win it,” said Gnabry (as captured b y @iMiaSanMia ). “You always wish that for a teammate. He had an incredible year. So for me, of course, he has done enough to win it. He’s a key player for us and has shown his quality. I really hope he wins it.” Bayern’s nasty history at French Football’s prized award ceremony haunts them still, but Harry Kane has the best chan ce to exorcise Die Rekordmeister’s Ballon d’Or demons. item.title: Nancy Lieberman gives Caitlin Clark a reminder every athlete needs
item.description: Nancy Lieberman gives Caitlin Clark a reminder every athlete needs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Caitlin Clark had plenty to celebrate after her 2026 season with the Indiana Fever . She averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game, helping Indiana finish 28-16 and secure the sixth seed in the playoffs. Clark ranked third in the WNBA in scoring and second in assists, becoming the first player in league history to finish in the top three in both categories. But the message she shared after the season was not a victory lap built around those numbers. Clark reflected on being healthy and getting to do what she loves after an injury-shortened 2025 campaign in which she appeared in only 13 games. That note resonated with Nancy Lieberman, the Hall of Famer known as “Lady Magic.” Lieberman responded with a wish for Clark’s happiness, health and peace. It was a brief message, but one that acknowledged the demands that come with being one of the most visible players in basketball. The weight of being the headline Clark’s profile means nearly every part of her season becomes a topic of discussion, from her production to the Fever’s playoff hopes. Indiana’s first-round loss to the Las Vegas Aces ended a campaign that had genuine championship expectations, but it did not erase what Clark accomplished individually. Lieberman understands the attention that comes with being a basketball star. She has spent decades in the sport as a player, coach and public voice, and has repeatedly supported Clark during moments when the young guard faced intense criticism. Her latest message was not about telling Clark what to fix or how to respond to the Fever’s playoff exit. It was a reminder that health and peace matter, too. That may sound simple, but athletes often face pressure to treat every season as a referendum on their value. MORE : Dream's Angel Reese made WNBA Finals history despite Game 1 loss Clark is already looking ahead Clark’s reflection also included a familiar sign of what comes next: she is ready to get back to work. The Fever guard expressed gratitude for the season while making it clear that she intends to keep building. That balance is part of what makes her story compelling. Clark can recognize the importance of getting through a season healthy while still being driven to improve. Indiana’s early exit gives the team plenty to address, but Clark’s 2026 performance reinforced why the Fever remain a major draw. Lieberman’s comment offered a human moment amid the stats and playoff analysis. Clark’s production tells fans how she played. Her message about health, and the support she received in response, showed what getting back to a full season meant to her. item.title: Even Tom Brady couldn’t believe officiating late in Packers-Lions game
item.description: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Even Tom Brady couldn’t believe officiating late in Packers-Lions game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers hit the road to take on the Detroit Lions in Motown during Week 7 which included controversial calls that had coach Matt LaFleur biting his tongue in a postgame press conference, before letting his true feelings slip. Packers star pass rusher Micah Parsons called out the refs after the game, and he also got support from Tom Brady on the day as the NFL legend shared his thoughts. The play happened when Packers defensive tackle Karl Brooks came marauding in on Lions QB Jared Goff. He hit Goff right as he released a pass downfield to tight end Sam LaPorta that was completed. Roughing the passer was called, but Brady didn’t see it. Tom Brady has had enough with the officiating. "My goodness. What is that?" "There's no way!" "It's definitely not roughing the passer." https://t.co/CtETYvi5D3 pic.twitter.com/a0JlJUylJM — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 25, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Green Bay continued to fight and took the Lions down to the wire before losing, 20-17. A missed field goal by rookie kicker Trey Smack opened the door for the Lions, who took advantage, driving for a game-winning Jake Bates field goal and sending Green Bay to 4-3 on the season. Running back Josh Jacobs’ status became a hot topic before the game and he was able to play, teaming with Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft to help Jordan Love excel in the passing game. Love had a rough play that he would like to take back, a deep ball that was snagged out of mid-air by Lions injury returnee Brian Branch . The Pack now finds itself behind the Lions, Bears and Vikings in a jam-packed NFC North division. All four teams have playoff hopes, but Green Bay’s suddenly appear a whole lot fainter after Week 7’s crushing loss. LaFleur and his team will do their best to avoid getting fined in the wake their hard-luck loss, with plenty of work left to do before the season ends. item.title: New York Jets vs. Las Vegas Raiders odds: Opening lines for Week 8 matchup
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 12: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs the ball during a game against the New York Jets at Allegiant Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets lost their second straight game against an AFC East opponent on Sunday. Last week the Jets lost a hard fought game to the defending AFC champions New England Patriots. That was understandable. Much less understandable was today’s 28 – 25 loss at home to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins dominated the action for most of the game, building a two touchdown lead at halftime and maintaining an 11 point lead with less than five minutes remaining in the game before a late Jets touchdown made the score look closer than the game actually was. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Their latest loss came at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams by a 35 – 21 score. The Raiders’ defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the Raiders making the long trip east for this game and suffering through the early game start, on paper this looks like a get well game for the Jets. However, the way the Jets are playing no game on the schedule should be looked at as an easy win. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think this game is close to a tossup. The current line has the Jets home favorites by 1.5 points. The game has an over/under of 44.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are -118 while the Dolphins are +100. Let’s see if the Jets can recover from a terrible loss and take care of business at home against the Raiders. J-E-T-S! item.description: COLUMBUS — You say you want a rematch, eh? You got your wish. Of the the five Muskingum Valley League teams that qualified for the high school football postseason, four will face rematch games in the first round. Another, New Lexington, received a first-round bye by virtue of its No. 2 seed in Division IV, Region 15. Pairings were announced officially by the Ohio High School Athletic Association on Oct. 25. More: Sheridan football comeback stuns unbeaten New Lex, Week 10 roundup More: Right on time, Reese St. Clair plays hero vs. Claymont football More: Philo tops Maysville, shares MVL title as Lincicome ties record Here is a look at the local matchups: Sheridan, Tri-Valley back in Region 11 field In Division III, Region 11, Sheridan (8-2) jumped into a first-round home game as the No. 6 seed following its Week 10 win against the Panthers. Its opponent is one all-too familiar — MVL rival Tri-Valley (7-3), in the playoffs for the seventh straight year and a team that handed the Generals a 38-21 defeat in Week 9. The Scotties are seeded 11th. The winner plays at No. 3 seed Columbus East (9-1), of the Columbus City League, which finished 9-1. That winner plays either No. 2 Licking Valley (10-0), No. 7 Granville (7-3) or No. 10 Plain City Jonathan Alder (7-3). The other half of the bracket features No. 1 Steubenville (8-2) hosting the winner of No. 8 Columbus Linden McKinley (9-1) and No. 9 Jackson (7-3), and No. 4 Athens (9-1) welcoming either No. 5 Dover (8-2) or No. 12 Columbus South (8-2). The Generals are in the postseason for the 25th time and ninth time in 11 years under coach Paul Culver III, which included a regional runner-up finish in 2023. He shot 17-of-30 from the field, including 8-of-18 from beyond the arc, and 10-of-11 from the free-throw line. Doncic reflected on the win after the game on the broadcast. He noted how he was willing to pass the ball to Reaves, even with his red-hot scoring night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I mean, he was wide open, and I missed the previous three, so he was wide open. He was a hack today. He had five fouls, but no. Overall, you know, we had a terrible first quarter, so that fight that came back in the second quarter helped us get this win,” Doncic said. "Played the basketball we know how to play. We learned our lesson, so we cannot start games like this anymore." Utah punched Los Angeles in the mouth to start, boasting a 47-29 lead in the first quarter. The Lakers fired back with 45 points in the second quarter, taking control of the momentum for the rest of the night. Five players scored in double-digits for Los Angeles in the win, including Doncic. Austin Reaves had a strong night with 29 points, four assists, two blocks, one rebound, and one steal. He shot 7-of-12 overall, including 4-of-5 from downtown, and 11-of-13 from the charity stripe. Collin Sexton came next with 13 points and two rebounds, Matisse Thybulle had 11 points and three steals, while Ziaire Williams provided 11 points and two rebounds. The Lakers will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Portland Trail Blazers as tip-off starts on Oct. 27 at 11 p.m. ET. item.title: Sophie Cunningham reveals a runway goal that would surprise Fever fans
item.description: Sophie Cunningham reveals a runway goal that would surprise Fever fans originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sophie Cunningham has a new goal for the future, and it has nothing to do with a jump shot. The Indiana Fever guard said on her “No Hesitation” podcast that she would love to become a Victoria’s Secret Angel one day. Cunningham brought up the idea while talking with co-host Drew Hanlen about the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. She was enthusiastic about the event, praising the models and describing the show as a major spectacle. She also singled out longtime Angel Candice Swanepoel as a favorite and complimented Kylie Jenner’s appearance. Then Cunningham offered a playful glimpse of her own ambition: she could picture herself on that runway someday, perhaps even alongside Hanlen’s wife, Christine Burke. The comment was lighthearted, but it fits a Fever guard who has never been shy about showing fans her personality away from basketball. Cunningham’s public profile has grown through her podcast, brand partnerships and modeling work, including an appearance in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition. Basketball still comes first Cunningham is coming off her second season with Indiana, where she averaged 7.9 points and 2.3 rebounds in 43 games. She was a regular part of the rotation, usually coming off the bench, and helped the Fever finish 28-16 before they lost to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs. Her next basketball chapter is still unsettled. Cunningham’s one-year contract with Indiana has expired, making her an unrestricted free agent this offseason. She could return to the Fever, sign elsewhere or weigh her options as teams begin shaping their 2027 rosters. That uncertainty makes her personal goal especially fun to consider. Cunningham has spoken about a possible runway future, but she has not announced a modeling contract or a move away from basketball. For now, it is an ambition she shared while discussing a fashion show she clearly enjoys. MORE : Angel Reese is turning three very different WNBA Finals games into the same result The Fever guard keeps fans guessing Cunningham’s mix of competitiveness and humor has helped make her one of the WNBA’s most recognizable personalities. She can be intense on the court, but she also gives fans plenty to follow when the season ends. A Victoria’s Secret runway appearance would be a dramatic new setting for the Fever guard, and Cunningham sounds as if she would embrace the challenge. For now, though, her immediate future includes free agency and whatever comes next in basketball. The runway dream is a reminder that Cunningham’s interests stretch well beyond the court. Whether that goal ever becomes reality, she has already made it clear she is comfortable being herself in front of an audience. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year. "So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep." Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. item.title: Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings
item.description: Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc were first and second at the US Grand Prix [Getty Images] Championship leader Kimi Antonelli sealed his ninth victory of the season with victory at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third. Mercedes' Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history if he finishes ninth or higher at the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Texas. Kimi Antonelli - 10/10 A superb weekend under the added pressure of having his first opportunity to seal the championship. Produced an outstanding lap for pole and then controlled the race beautifully, making the one-stop work while many around him needed two. Charles Leclerc - 9.5/10 Very close to a perfect weekend himself. He was given a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, which dropped him to 10th after his pit stop. He could only make up two places and finished eighth. Hamilton's fourth place means both he and fellow Briton Russell just about retain a mathematical chance of winning the championship. The entertainment was provided by Leclerc and Verstappen, initially wheel to wheel and then at a distance as divergent strategies played out. Leclerc, who started fourth, jumped up to third place behind Verstappen on the exit of the first corner, and then bravely sat it out around the outside of the Red Bull through the high speed Turn Three at the start of the Esses and then dived down the inside into Turn Four. Verstappen, though, was not finished, and he closed in on Leclerc down the back straight and they fought hard through the switchback series of corners through the stadium section before the Dutchman claimed second place with a dive down the inside of Turn 15. Verstappen led Leclerc to his first stop on lap 13, Ferrari waiting two laps longer before the Monegasque made his own first stop. Verstappen went on to the soft tyres and Leclerc the mediums, the Dutchman then switching to mediums when he stopped on lap 31. But Leclerc's mediums in the second stint allowed him to run eight laps longer than the Red Bull driver. Leclerc came out 8.5 seconds behind the Dutchman and closed the gap to be on his tail within five laps as Verstappen himself came up behind Lando Norris' McLaren. They ran nose to tail for two laps before Verstappen passed Norris into Turn One on lap 47, Leclerc following him past later in the lap. Verstappen was grumbling about his car over the radio for much of the race but he had enough to hold off a late charge from Hamilton - on a similar strategy to Leclerc - by one second at the flag. Norris managed to nurse his tyres to the end with just one stop to beat Hadjar, while the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri fended off Russell for half the race to take seventh. item.title: Packers’ Micah Parsons calls out NFL, officials amid wild 4th quarter vs. Lions
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers’ Micah Parsons calls out NFL, officials amid wild 4th quarter vs. Lions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers suffered a tough 20-17 loss at the hands of the Detroit Lions, who hit a walk-off field goal as time expired. The Lions were aided by a roughing the passer penalty on the Packers during second play of the final drive, which sent them on their way. Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons , who was not playing as he continues to rehab his knee injury, was not pleased by the call against his team. He went to X, formerly Twitter, to vent his frustration at the league and its officials . “Let’s just go to flag football if everytime a qb gets touched it’s roughing the passer!” Parsons wrote, tagging both the NFL and the NFL Officiating accounts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) As a pass rusher himself, Parsons should be keenly aware that the NFL has shifted toward protecting quarterbacks more in recent years. That includes having more roughing the passer penalties. It may be frustrating for pass rushers like Parsons, but it is just how the game is being officiated these days. But while the roughing the passer penalty was a blow to the Packers, they still had their chances to get the road win, which they did not capitalize on. Trey Smack’s two missed field goals – one at the start of the game and one that was blocked with the game tied – played a big part in their loss. Meanwhile, quarterback Jordan Love also threw a crucial interception in the fourth quarter with the Packers down 17-14. As for Parsons, the latest updates suggest he is still weeks away from getting back on the field for the Packers this season. So in the meantime, expect some more social media commentary from him during Packers games. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
